by the Civil Service Act (22 Stat. 403)  
and by section 1753 of the Revised  
Statutes of the United States (U.S.C.,

appointing officer shall make selections  
for the first vacancy from not more than

be made and sustained by the Commis­

tions in Federal agencies concerned in  
preparedness and the national defense  
program, for such other reasons as may  
be approved by the Commission.”

research_rationale: EO 8423 (signed 1940-05-28, 5 FR 2099, FR issue of 1940-06-01), read in full from the held official FR text: one operative paragraph rewriting the first sentence of Rule VII sec. 2(b). It is revoked by number in EO 9830 Part III, effective 1947-05-01 (the enacting clause 'effective May 1, 1947' governs Part III; signing and FR filing on 1947-02-24 are not the effective date). The ACT record ACT:EO:8423>EO:9830 is an agent-located record upheld by an independent AI reviewer with a D6 step (simulated ingestion; not yet in the committed build). D6 / earlier-end test (did any instrument other than EO 9830 end the order or a clause before 1947-05-01?): The order has no sunset, term or termination clause of its own; the words 'positions in Federal agencies concerned in preparedness and the national defense program' limit the objection grounds, not the life of the order. The by-number scan of held FR order texts 1940-1947 finds 8423 only in EO 9830 (its Part III row and the codification table) and in the FR pages shared with EO 8424/8425; the other hits are commodity table numbers in EO 8702/8703. Every held 1940-1947 'Rule VII' hit was read: EO 8424/8425 (same FR issue), and EO 9428 (1944-02-29), which only refers to Rule VII when granting status to certain fingerprint classifiers and does not amend sec. 2(b). 'Highest three' hits: EO 8576 (separate regulations for unclassified positions) and the War Service Regulations sec. 18.4(c) as amended (held in EO_9524.txt), a parallel selection rule for war-service appointments under EO 9063 that neither names nor amends Rule VII sec. 2(b) (scope lead, not an end). EO 9691 (1946-02-04, held, read) directs that within thirty days all classified-service actions 'shall be made in accordance with the Civil Service Rules and Regulations', which presupposes Rule VII as amended remained in force. No earlier end of the order or of any clause was found, so every clause is terminated on 1947-05-01 and no later event is attached. Savings: none_after_bounded_search (see savings_residuals). AI producer hypothesis only; not human certification and not a status.

savings_residuals.reason: Reading record for EO 9830 (held FR text jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_9830.txt, text_sha256 b519c570..., 12 FR 1259 ff., read for this purpose: enacting clause, Parts I-III and every revocation row): the enacting clause 'it is hereby ordered as follows, effective May 1, 1947:' (offsets 2164-2220) governs Parts I (Civil Service Rules), II (Schedules) and III; Part III (from offset 90277) is the single sentence 'The following Executive orders are hereby revoked:' followed by a one-per-line list of orders, with no exception, savings, pending-matter or 'nothing herein' wording; a search of the whole text for 'shall not affect', 'heretofore', 'pending', 'nothing herein', 'remain in effect', 'continue in effect' and 'supersed' finds no savings clause for revoked orders (the only 'heretofore' hit, at 30777, concerns persons appointed under the new Rule III sec. 3.2). Own-residual check, reading EO 8423 in full: it set the rule of selection from certificates; selections made under it before 1947-05-01 are completed appointments that rest on the appointing authority, not continuing effects of the order. EO 9830 contains no 'highest three' wording (searched); its new sec. 4.3 (offset 31973) only says the appointing officer fills positions from a certificate of eligibles 'solely on the basis of merit and fitness', a general new rule, not a continuation of EO 8423. EO 9830 has no savings clause reaching it. Nothing of the order outlives its revocation. Bounded search: the order and EO 9830 read in full in the held official FR texts; a by-number scan of all 6,652 held FR order texts (jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts; every hit read in context); the OFR catalog edges for the order (jobs/later-events EDGES.csv); a check of catalog titles of unheld orders between the order and EO 9830 for any personnel-rule change; the three machine searches (OFR catalog, U.S. Code, eCFR) read with their scope notes.

At a session of the Civil Aeronautics  
Authority held at its office in Washing­
ton, D. C., on the 28th day of May, 1940.
Acting pursuant to the authority vested  
in it by the Civil Aeronautics Act of 1938,  
particularly sections 205 (a), 601, 603,  
604, and 605 of said Act, and finding that
its action is desirable in the public inter­
est and is necessary to carry out the  
provisions of and to exercise and perform  
its powers and duties under said Act, the  
Civil Aeronautics Authority adopts the  
following amendment to the Civil Air  
Regulations:
Effective July 1, 1940, Parts 04 and 40  
of the Civil Air Regulations are amended  
as follows:
1. By amending § 04.430 to read as fol­
lows:
“§  04.430 Installation.  All control  
systems and operating devices shall be  
so designed and installed as to provide  
reasonable ease of operation by the crew  
and so as to preclude the probability of  
inadvertent operation, jamming, chaf­
ing, interference by cargo, passengers or  
loose objects, and the slapping of cables  
against parts of the airplane. All pul­
leys shall be provided with satisfactory  
guards.”
2. By amending §  04.701 to read as  
follows:
“§  04.701 Take-off.  Take-off at sea  
level:
“(a) Within 1,000 feet for land planes;
“(b) Within 60 seconds in calm air  
for seaplanes.”
3. By amending §  04.702 to read as  
follows:
“§  04.702 Climb. The average rate of  
climb for the first minute after the air­
plane leaves the take-off surface in ac­
cordance with §  04.701, and the rate of  
steady climb at sea level with not more  
than maximum except take-off power,  
shall not be less in feet per minute than:
“(a) Land planes.  Eight times the  
measured power-off stalling speed in  
miles per hour with the flaps and land­
ing gear retracted, or 300 feet per min­
ute, whichever is greater;
“(b) Sea planes.  Six times the meas­
ured power-off stalling sped in miles per  
hour with the flaps retracted, or 250  
feet per minute, whichever is greater.”

§§ 04.710 to 04.714, inclusive) to read as  
follows:

requirements of Part 61 may be in­
creased beyond the values correspond­
ing to the landing speed specified in  
§  04.700 and take-off requirements of  
§  04.701, subject to the following condi­
tions:”

follows:
